The next assignment is to derive the regularized Sonin trace formula while retaining an explicit boundary correction. I’ve started two parallel checks of the projection formula and its trace conditions. I’ll preserve the existing changes and save the derivation and a separate critical review in the repository.

The derivation has a promising form: the phase contribution gives exactly the gamma term minus the regularized prime sum, while the projection adds explicit cutoff and resolvent terms. Those terms retain the boundary correction. I’m checking that each trace is legitimate and that the correction recovers the known archimedean error when the prime weights vanish.

The checks also give a useful extension: the phase family has finite traces on every compact frequency window, even where the full source-smoothed trace is still unproved. The remaining issue is the boundary term’s limit and the frequency tails. Below \(\sigma=1\), the phase term also cannot be identified with the finite prime deformation without accounting for pole and zero crossings.

The derivation is saved and has passed two separate internal mathematical checks. It gives an explicit boundary formula, a controlled return expansion for \(\sigma>1\), and a positive family with compact frequency cutoffs. I’m updating the project overview to record the remaining task: control the boundary’s limiting behavior and the frequency tails, then identify the complete arithmetic form.

For \(\sigma>1\), the result is
\[
B_\sigma=\Gamma-W_\sigma+K_\sigma,
\]
with an explicit boundary-resolvent correction recovering \(E_\infty\). The analysis also establishes local frequency-trace finiteness beyond that region.

The remaining work is controlling the boundary limit and frequency tails, then identifying the complete arithmetic form—including pole and zero-crossing contributions. No arithmetic limit or RH proof is claimed.

I’ll continue from the new boundary formula, focusing first on the cutoff spectral tail and whether the full boundary contribution can be controlled near the critical endpoint. I’ll check the arithmetic crossing terms in parallel, so any limiting claim keeps the complete Weil form in view.

There is a useful distinction emerging. The frequency tails may admit a uniform bound using local zeta-zero counts, which would settle full trace finiteness. But an exact comparison model shows that the right local phase concentration can coexist with a zero Sonin projection: the boundary can cancel all of it. I’m separating what can be proved for the actual zeta family from what still needs control of its exact intersection space.

The tail argument now checks: near \(\sigma=\tfrac12\), each unit frequency window has a uniform \(O(\log^2(2+|t|))\) trace bound. This establishes full smoothed-trace finiteness and controls the tails for every compact smooth source.

The remaining uncertainty is more specific: return mass can concentrate at cutoff spectral value \(1\) and remove part of the critical-line trace. The comparison model shows why strong convergence and local phase data alone cannot exclude that loss.

The results are saved, and the combined internal review found no unresolved correction. For prepared sources, the remaining discrepancy is now explicit:
\[
B_\sigma-Q=-R_\sigma-Z_{\mathrm{off}}+o(1),\qquad R_\sigma\ge0.
\]
Here \(R_\sigma\) is the return defect and \(Z_{\mathrm{off}}\) is the complete signed off-line zero pairing. The open step is determining which critical-line modes survive in the actual zeta projection’s exact kernel; the finiteness and tail estimates are now established.
